preamble: Fricativization of the close back rounded vowel [u] to the labiodental fricative [f]. Cappadocian Greek shows the one generally acknowledged case, in the plural of 'ear': earlier ta otjá > ta utjá > ta ftjá, from which a new singular to ftí was formed. Janse & Vandewalle (2020) consider the same high-vowel fricativization for ta ušáxja > ta fšáxja 'the children', but also derive that word from Old Turkish uvşak by apheresis, so it is not counted here.

examples.note: Unstressed [u] became [f] before voiceless [t]; the singular to ftí 'the ear' was then made by back-formation.

sources: Janse, Mark, & Vandewalle, Johan (2020). The History and Etymology of Cappadocian fšáx 'Child', Pharasiot fšáxi 'Boy'. Transactions of the Philological Society 118(3), 500–514. https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-968X.12202
